long_biography.plain_text:
King Hamad's National Action Charter placed constitutional change at the centre of Bahrain's political settlement after he became ruler. Approved by referendum, it preceded the kingdom's 2002 constitution, restoration of an elected lower house and full political rights for women. These measures define the early reform programme of his reign, alongside his continuing role in Bahrain's regional diplomacy.

History and national heritage have been a sustained personal interest. While crown prince, Hamad directed the creation of the Historical Documents Centre and later brought it within his court. He also wrote First Light: Modern Bahrain and Its Heritage, combining historical study with an account of the country's military development. The centre now supports researchers and preserves documentary material on Bahrain's past.
